experiments.name: dependent chain
experiments.asm: fdiv.s $f0, $f0, $f1; fdiv.s $f0, $f0, $f1; movfr2gr.s $r4, $f0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; movgr2fr.w $f0, $r4
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 2000 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 1065353216; movgr2fr.w $f0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1065353216; movgr2fr.w $f1, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0' --asm 'fdiv.s $f0, $f0, $f1; fdiv.s $f0, $f0, $f1; movfr2gr.s $r4, $f0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; movgr2fr.w $f0, $r4'

latencies.notes: Data-dependent latency: 8 cycles for 0/0, x/0, 0/x, Inf/NaN; 10 for 1/1 and 1/2; 16 for general quotients; 15 for 1/max; 9 for max/minnorm or minnorm/max; 17 for 1/maxsub. Measured with an integer-bit reset chain; 5 cycles of helper latency are subtracted. The sample experiment uses 1.0.

notes: Latency model: 8 cycles for special operands, 10 when the divisor is a power of two (the stored sample uses 1.0/1.0), 16 for a general divisor, up to +1 with a subnormal operand. The stored experiment runs the division twice, so cycles = (core_cycles - 6) / 2. 64-bit vector lanes match the scalar numbers and run in parallel (slowest lane dominates); 32-bit vector lanes cost 2 x scalar - 5.
